question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Spinning one’s wheels

options.text: To do a lot of work for achieving something
To make a lot of effort without achieving anything
To talk about oneself for achieving something

solution:
The correct answer is **"To make a lot of effort without achieving anything."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"spinning one's wheels"** means to exert a lot of effort or energy without making any progress or achieving anything. (कोई प्रगति किए बिना या कुछ भी हासिल किए बिना बहुत अधिक प्रयास या ऊर्जा लगाना)

 
 
• **Example**: *I sat in front of the computer all night trying to write, but I felt like I was just **spinning my wheels**__.*
 
 
 
• **Spinning one’s wheels** means to make a lot of effort without achieving anything.
 
• The correct option is Option 2, which accurately reflects this meaning.
